business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Africa (national unitary jurisdiction; exclusive company registry authority vested in the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); no sub-state registries)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Roman-Dutch common law overlaid by English corporate-law heritage, with constitutional supremacy under the Constitution, 1996; corporate law codified in the Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment (2006)
African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement (2019, in force for South Africa)
DTAA with the United States of America (2005)
DTAA with the United Kingdom (2002, as amended 2014)
DTAA with the People's Republic of China (2000)
DTAA with the Republic of India (1997)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss50–50D as substituted and inserted by the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024 (commenced 27 December 2024); Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R351 of 26 April 2011), as amended by GN 609 of 2023 (beneficial ownership); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the FIC Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorism and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); FIC directives and guidance notes on beneficial ownership and client due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of director and shareholder identity documents (valid passport or South African ID), with apostille for non-resident documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African Commissioner of Oaths/Notary Public; for non-residents, notary of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (South Africa acceded 1995; DIRCO or competent foreign apostille authority); no consular legalization required for Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address for each director and beneficial owner (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank; certification by Commissioner of Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued outside South Africa; domestic certified copy if issued in South Africa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate extract of any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization where the foreign state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A or bespoke MOI), including executed signature pages of incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: CIPC e-filing; foreign signature pages notarized and apostilled if executed abroad; bank accounts will require a certified copy within 3 months

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing a local incorporation agent (if directors sign outside South Africa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation risk-based screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) South African FIC sanctions list and domestic terrorist designations under POCDATARA; (iii) OFAC SDN List; (iv) UK/EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; and (v) PEP databases covering FICA ss28A–28B domestic and foreign prominent public officials, including family members and close associates. Screening must be repeated on trigger events and at least annually per FICA risk-based standards, with records retained 5 years under FICA s43(1). The entity will also be subjected to refreshed KYC/AML due diligence by accountable institutions onboarding the payment rails (Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments), which will require production of the CIPC-filed beneficial ownership register. Low-risk standard e-commerce tier does not exempt statutory FICA obligations of those institutions; the company must maintain a contemporaneous, filed UBO register within 10 business days of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Business Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za) — Company Name Reservation application (Form CoR 9.1)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Companies Act s11 and Companies Regulations 12–13, the name must be alpha-numeric in Latin (Roman) script, may be in any of South Africa's 11 official languages, must commence with a letter, must comprise no more than two name expressions, must not consist solely of a surname or initials without approval, must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered name or trademark, and must carry the mandatory suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or '(Pty) Ltd'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reserved name is valid for 60 calendar days and may be extended once for a further 60 days upon application and prescribed fee before expiry. On rejection, CIPC issues a refusal notice citing the statutory ground (e.g., s11(2) confusing similarity, or s11(3) prohibited expression). The applicant may (i) file an application with the Companies Tribunal under s160 for a name-determination order, (ii) request reconsideration under Companies Regulation 142 where applicable, or (iii) lodge a fresh CoR 9.1 with a modified name. Judicial review of an adverse CIPC decision lies in the High Court under s12(3). The reservation is automatically consumed upon successful incorporation and registration of the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted subject to substantive compliance with Companies Act s23: the registered office must be a physical South African address open to the public for not less than 2 hours on each ordinary business day during business hours, with document-access and mail-handling capability. A licensed virtual office or professional registered-office service provider meeting the 2-hour public-access test is acceptable for a low-risk fast-fashion e-commerce retailer; a bare postal box or virtual address without a staffed physical desk is non-compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (10–20% within the first 24 months): CIPC conducts risk-based inspections under s183, and the FIC targets accountable institutions; an e-commerce apparel retailer with a professional registered-office provider and an accurate filed UBO register faces minimal but non-zero unannounced inspection risk. All statutory records must be accessible at the registered office during the daily statutory window.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name reservation — two preferred name applications (Form CoR 9.1)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC Statutory Fee Schedule — ZAR 50 per name (≈USD 2.70 each); non-refundable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC company incorporation — single class of shares, standard MOI (CoR 15.1A, CoR 14.1, CoR 14.1A, CoR 14.2)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC Statutory Fee Schedule — ZAR 175 incorporation fee inclusive of name registration; ZAR 125 if incorporated without a registered name

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC initial beneficial ownership filing (Form CoR 55.1B) — bundled statutory fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: CIPC does not levy a separate statutory fee for the initial beneficial ownership filing; mandatory within 10 business days of incorporation under s50B of the Companies Amendment Act 16 of 2024. Professional preparation time is covered under external counsel line.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional registered office and corporate secretarial services (first 12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a CIPC-compliant physical office with 2-hour daily public access, mail handling, and regulatory correspondence — ZAR 3,000 (≈USD 162) per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO disclosure and PEP/sanctions screening pack (all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: In-house compliance team or external screening vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for FICA-aligned automated screening against UN/OFAC/FIC/EU/UK lists with manual review and 5-year record-keeping — ZAR 1,200 (≈USD 65)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and certification of identity, address, and director consent documents (estimated 4 notarial acts)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Legal Practice Council notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark — ZAR 750 (≈USD 40.50)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: DIRCO apostille legalization of foreign documents (estimated 3 documents for non-resident directors/shareholders)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO) — Legalisation Service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: DIRCO legalisation fee schedule — ZAR 150 per apostille (≈USD 8.10); excludes courier fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External attorney fees — pre-incorporation due diligence, MOI drafting, name clearance monitoring, and incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard private company (Pty) Ltd incorporation without bespoke shareholder provisions — ZAR 2,500 (≈USD 135)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; ss 13(1) (incorporation), 19(1)(b) (legal personality), 66(1) (board of directors) and 70 (company secretary).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares must be issued for adequate consideration as required by s 40 of the Companies Act, with a valuation report for non-cash consideration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers hereby subscribe for the shares allotted to them under the Memorandum of Incorporation and are registered as members of the Company. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], and that the books and records be kept at that address. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed as the sole director of the Company, and [Name] as the Company Secretary, each with full authority to open bank accounts, file regulatory documents, and execute all ancillary agreements. RESOLVED that all actions taken by subscribers in registering the Company are ratified and confirmed. RESOLVED that this resolution be recorded and take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application (Form CoR 9.1) via the CIPC transactional portal. Ensure the proposed name is not undesirable or confusingly similar to existing registrations. Simultaneously prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) in the prescribed standard form or a custom MOI containing governance provisions.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of ID or passport of each subscriber/incorporator
Proof of residential or business address of subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused or objected to, file a new name reservation with further distinguishing elements or submit a formal objection/appeal to CIPC within 20 business days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and lodge the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the executed MOI, using the CIPC online filing system. Pay the prescribed incorporation fee and electronically attach the name reservation approval, director consents, and subscriber declarations.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 14.1 including incorporator and director details
Signed consent to act as director (Form CoR 14.1A)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects or queries the filing, correct the identified defects within 20 business days by resubmitting the amended CoR 14.1 and supporting documents without additional penalty; if prolonged, escalate via CIPC customer support or legal representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of incorporation certificate and initial governance filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC (automated/system generated) and board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (CORP ID). Convene a board meeting or pass written board resolutions to adopt the MOI, issue share certificates to subscribers, appoint auditors or a reporting accountant if required, and establish the registered address.
required_dossiers: Board meeting minutes or written resolutions
Registered office confirmation notice (CoR 14.3, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains incorrect particulars, file a correction application under s 24 of the Companies Act with CIPC, attaching statutory declarations and a rectification fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and employment registration with SARS and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) and Compensation Fund (DOEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, Value-Added Tax (VAT) if taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed R1 million per annum, Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), and UIF as an employer. Use the SARS eFiling portal to complete the relevant registration forms (e.g., VAT101, EMP101). Also register for the Compensation Fund if any employees are hired.
required_dossiers: Certified ID copies of all directors and the public officer (if appointed)
Completed SARS registration forms (VAT101, EMP101, IT/company registration)
Details of registered office and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS delays the tax registration or queries a form, submit a written escalation via the SARS eFiling secure messaging, provide any additional declarations, and if unresolved within 21 days, lodge a service complaint with the SARS Tax Ombud.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not required — no industrial or manufacturing activity; if a physical warehouse is established, the local municipality (e.g., Johannesburg Metro) may require a business/trading license under by-laws.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Non-applicable for pure e-commerce retail; no operating license required under the National Business Act, 1996 or any industrial licensing regime.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (electronic retail activities are not listed in the EIA Regulations 2014, Listing Notices 1–3; no full EIA or environmental authorization required)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to non-manufacturing retail. If warehousing or logistics operations are later added, comply with the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act (Act 39 of 2004) and National Water Act (Act 36 of 1998) for any controlled emissions, effluent discharge, or waste generated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No fire safety certificate or structural load inspection required for a purely online retail office. If a fulfilment centre or retail store is opened, obtain a Certificate of Compliance under the National Building Regulations (SANS 10400) and comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Act 85 of 1993) for fire prevention, emergency exits, and workplace safety inspections by the Department of Employment and Labour.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS), with mandatory electronic filing through the SARS eFiling portal (https://efiling.sars.gov.za); customs and export control administered by the SARS Customs and Excise division.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Incorporate the entity at the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) or, for a non-resident trading entity, register as an external company; (2) apply to SARS via eFiling for the enterprise income tax reference number (TIN) within 21 business days of incorporation or commencement of business (Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, s 22), submitting the CIPC registration certificate, certified director identification/passports and proof of registered address; (3) once taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period, lodge the VAT 101 registration application (with VAT 101A/B enterprise and bank schedules) electronically; foreign electronic-service suppliers must additionally file the relevant SARS non-resident vendor declaration and designate a SARS address of service in South Africa; (4) concurrently register for PAYE, UIF and SDL if employees are engaged; (5) upon approval, SARS issues a VAT vendor number (format 4XXXXXXXXX) and the 15-digit tax reference number, after which eFiling profiles, Tax Compliance Status (TCS) and binding private rulings become available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A ZA-resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed as a separate entity on worldwide income at the standard corporate rate of 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; foreign shareholders are not taxed at entity level but face 20% dividends withholding tax on distributions unless the participation exemption applies. Territorial_Scope: residence (incorporation or Place of Effective Management) triggers worldwide taxation; non-resident companies are taxed only on South African-source income, including deemed-source income for e-commerce services under Income Tax Act s 9(2)(l). Tax_Exempt_Zone: not generally applicable; Special Economic Zone (SEZ) incentives are preferential but do not confer a blanket exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no US-style check-the-box election; classification follows legal form. Relevant elections available to a foreign-owned e-commerce group: (1) headquarter company status election under Income Tax Act s 9I (first-return election permitting certain foreign dividends, interest, royalties and controlled-company income to flow through on a tax-neutral basis); (2) controlled foreign company (CFC) participation-exemption positions under s 9D; (3) hybrid instrument and hybrid mismatch ordering elections under ss 8E, 8EA, 23M and 23N (BEPS Action 2 ordering); (4) VAT group registration election under VAT Act s 50 for associated companies to file as a single vendor; and (5) s 11D research-and-development allowance election for qualifying scientific expenditure.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS as the national indirect tax authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 (compulsory VAT registration when taxable supplies exceed R1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted once taxable turnover exceeds R50,000; foreign suppliers of electronic services are deemed to carry on an enterprise in South Africa and are subject to the same R1,000,000 registration threshold notwithstanding any physical-presence requirement)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance hub, digital stamping or mandatory QR-code regime is currently operational in South Africa. SARS requires all VAT returns (VAT 201) to be filed through eFiling and requires electronic tax invoices to satisfy VAT Act s 20(4) content requirements (vendor name and VAT number, tax invoice number, date of supply, goods description, consideration and VAT amount where applicable). SARS has announced a phased mandatory e-invoicing roadmap (SARS eInvoicing) for high-turnover vendors, which will require digitally signed invoices and machine-readable data transmission via the SARS eFiling/API environment. Until activation of that mandate, proof of export is maintained in the vendor export register and exchanged electronically with SARS customs (SAD500) and the authorised dealer bank.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under VAT Act s 11(1)(a), the supply of movable goods (including fast-fashion apparel and footwear) is zero-rated where the goods are exported by the vendor within 90 days of the time of supply and the vendor retains the full prescribed proof-of-export records. Cross-border services supplied to non-residents (e.g., e-commerce platform and related inbound logistics services for offshore customers) qualify for zero-rating under s 11(2)(l), provided the recipient is outside South Africa and the services are not physically rendered in South Africa. Domestic B2C/B2B supplies to South African customers remain standard-rated at 15%, and goods imported into South Africa for fulfilment are subject to VAT at importation (15% plus customs duty where applicable).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SARS SAD500 full export entry or electronic cargo-exit declaration submitted through the Customs EDI platform)
Bill of Lading or Airway Waybill (alternatively courier delivery confirmation evidencing physical dispatch out of South Africa)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the authorised dealer (foreign-currency bank settlement proof linked to the export transaction)
Commercial invoice and packing list with matched HS codes, quantities, weight and declared value
Proof-of-Export register (SARS VAT 264 or equivalent export sales journal) demonstrating export within the 90-day statutory period
Foreign customer order and payment-settlement records, including the BNPL/settlement statement where payment is routed through Klarna or Shopify Payments
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS reconciles customs SAD500 data with VAT 201 returns and bank settlement data; if export conditions are not met (including failure to export goods within 90 days or defective documentation), the zero-rating is reversed and output VAT is assessed at 15% with interest under Tax Administration Act s 187. Under TAA ss 222-223, understatement penalties escalate from 10% (substantial understatement) to 25% (failure to take reasonable care), 50% (position without reasonable grounds), 100% (gross negligence) and 150% (intentional tax evasion); criminal prosecution under TAA s 234 and the Customs and Excise Act 91 of 1964 may follow for fraudulent export declarations, with asset seizure, director disqualification and publication of the taxpayer name on the SARS defaulters list. Unrepatriated export proceeds beyond the 180-day deadline attract exchange-control corrective measures and penalties under the Currency and Exchanges Manual administered through the authorised dealer.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB); exchange control is administered by SARB's Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, through authorised dealers (resident commercial banks licensed under the Banks Act, 1990); the Prudential Authority supervises banking institutions, and SARS administers customs, import/export declarations, transfer-pricing and tax-clearance reporting that interact with cross-border treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is a managed-float, CLS-eligible currency that is freely convertible for current-account items — trade in goods and services, e-commerce platform payouts (Shopify Payments, Klarna BNPL settlements), interest, and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders — provided each transaction is executed through an authorised dealer with verified supporting documentation and the correct SARB balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical coding. Capital-account items, notably resident offshore treasury, shareholder loans to foreign group entities, and outward portfolio investment, are restricted and require prior FinSurv approval, an applicable authorised-dealer delegated limit, or a SARS tax-clearance certificate. For a fast-fashion e-commerce importer/retailer (ISIC 4791), ordinary trade payables, consumer-payout receipts, and profit remittances are current-account in nature; the principal convertibility hurdles are (i) retention of offshore PSP balances beyond approved settlement windows without a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) approval, (ii) transfer-pricing scrutiny on the margin embedded in cross-border apparel sourcing, and (iii) documentary mismatches between PSP settlement records and customs bills of entry that cause an authorised dealer to suspend payout crediting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual, proceeds from exported goods must be received in South Africa within 90 days from the date of shipment (extendable to 180 days with authorised-dealer or FinSurv approval in defined cases); all receipts must be surrendered to an authorised dealer — i.e., converted/credited to a ZAR account — unless FinSurv has approved a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) retention facility; the effective statutory conversion ratio for export receivables is therefore 100%. In the platform model, where offshore PSPs such as Shopify Payments and Klarna collect end-customer proceeds on the entity's behalf, the same surrender discipline applies: net settlement flows must be swept to the ZAR operational account, traceable to order-level e-commerce data within the settlement-cycle terms disclosed to the authorised dealer; any offshore retention requires a documented business case and FCA approval, not merely a balance held on an EMI dashboard.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank / Rand Merchant Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance (Commercial LC) Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM as a primary operating bank. Non-resident digital banks and e-money institutions (UK/FCA EMIs, EU EMIs, offshore payment fintechs) are not authorised dealers under South African exchange control, cannot clear ZAR through the SAMOS RTGS system, and cannot lawfully receive or hold export proceeds that are subject to the SARB surrender rules. Such rails are viable only as complementary payout/collection services — e.g., Shopify Balance, Wise Business, Klarna settlement accounts — provided funds are swept promptly and traceably to a Tier-1 ZAR operational account. A SARB-licensed digital bank resident in South Africa (e.g., TymeBank, Bank Zero) may facilitate eKYC onboarding but generally lacks integrated cross-border treasury, commercial LC, and forward-FX infrastructure; the optimal stack is therefore a Tier-1 commercial bank as the authorised-dealer anchor with fintech rails limited to the consumer-payment layer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (FICA) and FIC/Prudential Authority directives, there is no universal statutory mandate that directors appear physically; fully remote onboarding with liveness biometrics and interactive video verification is possible for a domestic (Pty) Ltd with resident directors. In practice, Tier-1 banks require an in-person or live-video interview of at least one director and the material ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) where (i) any director or UBO is a non-resident, (ii) the account receives pooled proceeds from payment aggregators such as Klarna and Shopify Payments, or (iii) the initial share capital is sourced from outside South Africa. Recommended blueprint: the principal executive director attends a physical onboarding/KYC meeting at the commercial desk of the chosen Tier-1 bank to accelerate credit approval, e-channel signing, and FX-dealing limits, while all other directors complete verified eKYC remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) opacity arising from nominee shareholders, inheritance-trust structures, or a foreign holding company in the ownership chain of the (Pty) Ltd.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC securities-register extract and beneficial-ownership filing (Companies Act, 2008, as amended by the General Laws Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing Amendment Act, 2022); an annotated group-structure chart from the (Pty) Ltd to every natural person; certified passport/ID copies of all UBOs and signatories; share certificates; and a sworn director's affidavit attesting that no undisclosed UBO or bearer-share arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment (TPP) aggregation risk: Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments pool settlement funds with other merchants, obscuring source-of-funds and creating a TPP red flag in the bank's AML engine.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PSP/merchant agreements with Shopify (Shopify Commerce B.V./Shopify Inc.) and Klarna; order-level settlement statements and payout schedules reconciling gross sales, refunds, chargebacks, and net funds; automated CRM/order exports linking each payout to consumer orders; PCI-DSS and SOC 2 attestations from the PSPs; a visual flow-of-funds diagram; and a board-approved policy committing to sweep all PSP balances to the ZAR operational account within the contractual settlement cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP hits: adverse-media or consolidated-list matches on directors, UBOs, counterparties, or end-customers accessing the storefront from embargoed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent consolidated-list screening (UN, EU, UK, OFAC) for all directors, UBOs, and the entity; signed PEP declarations and risk-rated due diligence on exposed relationships; Shopify/IP-geolocation geo-blocking evidence demonstrating exclusion of prohibited jurisdictions; an AML/CFT escalation and remediation manual; and, where a confirmed hit arises, a defensible suspicious-transaction report coordinated with the bank's compliance officer under section 29 of the FIC Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-profile mismatch: high-frequency, low-value e-commerce flows inconsistent with the stated business plan, or capital injections disproportionate to the operating scale (structuring/layering indicators).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved 12-month budget and sales forecast; historical platform analytics; executed supplier purchase orders for apparel/footwear sourcing; ERP and inventory reconciliation reports including courier and express-shipment statuses; and source-of-wealth evidence for capital above ZAR 10 million (founder tax returns, sale agreements, gift/inheritance declarations, or audited shareholder financials).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward-remittance financing red flags: a non-resident shareholder wiring the share subscription from a high-risk jurisdiction, or involvement of crypto/token rails or unrelated third-party payers in the capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement and board allotment resolution; SWIFT MT103 evidencing debit from the shareholder's own bank account; updated securities register; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth files; constitutional documents and audited financials of any offshore holding shareholder; the authorised dealer's inward-FDI reporting worksheet; and, where relevant, a SARS tax-clearance certificate or applicable exemption for the allotment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident equity subscriptions are structured as SWIFT MT103 payments (with MT202 cover where bank-to-bank credit is routed) into the (Pty) Ltd's Capital Escrow Account or designated ZAR operational account at an authorised dealer; the remittance must bear the purpose/BOP statistical code for inward direct investment (non-resident participation in share capital) and the narrative 'ZA_PTY_LTD — share subscription' referencing the subscription agreement and board resolution. No prior SARB approval is required for a plain non-resident equity injection into an authorised share class, but the authorised dealer will not finalise credit until it has verified the subscription documents, source-of-funds, sanctions screening, CIPC beneficial-ownership position, and, where triggered, the SARS tax-clearance certificate. Shareholder loans must be evidenced by a written loan agreement, bear arm's-length interest, and be recorded for exchange-control repatriation (repayment of principal and interest is a current-account item requiring authorised-dealer documentation). PSP settlement inflows from Klarna and Shopify are routed through the same authorised dealer as BOP service/merchandise flows with platform settlement reports attached.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements to offshore apparel and footwear suppliers (Bangladesh, Vietnam, China, Turkey) are executed via (i) SWIFT MT103/gpi open-account wire transfers against commercial invoices and packing lists; (ii) commercial letters of credit (MT700, governed by UCP600) for larger seasonal purchase orders requiring documentary security; (iii) documentary collections (documents against payment/acceptance) as a cost-sensitive intermediate; and (iv) spot or forward ZAR/FX conversion at the authorised dealer with a written rate confirmation. Local disbursements (logistics, warehousing, salaries, VAT, and interbank payments) clear through the South African Multiple Option Settlement (SAMOS) RTGS system using host-to-host banking APIs. Because ZAR is a CLS-eligible currency, USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, and GBP/ZAR cross-currency legs can achieve CLS payment-versus-payment settlement, eliminating Herstatt risk on the FX transaction. Refunds and chargebacks to consumers are funded from a dedicated PSP float account and reconciled monthly so that pooled gateway funds are never used for treasury speculation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) in USD/ZAR, EUR/ZAR, and GBP/ZAR concluded with a licensed authorised dealer, supported by genuine underlying import purchase orders or export receivables.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in ZAR, permissible for non-resident counterparties and for resident corporate hedges where FinSurv and authorised-dealer rules permit an NDF as a substitute for an onshore deliverable FEC.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) and bespoke currency swaps to convert and service a USD working-capital facility used for seasonal apparel inventory purchases.
European-style FX options with an authorised dealer to hedge timing risk on uncertain e-commerce cash-flow conversion windows and supplier payment dates.
Multi-currency pooling and hedging accounts at authorised dealers that allow the sweep of Shopify and Klarna multi-currency settlement balances into a single hedged ZAR conversion programme.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, s33; CIPC Form CoR 36.1 / CoR 36.1AET) — declaration of directors, shareholding, registered office, principal business and beneficial-ownership confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation: filing opens on the first day of the anniversary month and must be submitted within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CIPC compliance notice (Form DCF3) and a 'non-compliant' company status; failure to file for two consecutive years exposes the company to administrative strike-off/deregistration under s82(4)(b); directors may incur personal liability; the company cannot obtain a Certificate of Good Standing or renew operational licences; restoration after deregistration requires a court application or prescribed CIPC process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (BOR) — establishment, annual confirmation and change notifications, including share-transfer events, under s50 Companies Act 2008 as amended by the General Laws (AML & CTF) Amendment Act 22 of 2022.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) via Forms CoR 40.1 (BOR establishment/notice) and CoR 40.2 (declaration confirming BOR position).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: BOR must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of establishment; every change in beneficial ownership (e.g., a share transfer) must be filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the register amendment; annual confirmation is submitted together with the Annual Return inside the 30-business-day anniversary window.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC rejects the Annual Return and records the company as non-compliant; a compliance notice is issued; directors providing false or incomplete BOR information commit an offence under s214/s216, with fines and/or imprisonment; continuing default supports strike-off and prevents good-standing certification required by payment providers (Shopify Payments, Klarna BNPL).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) — prepared, board-approved and signed under s30 Companies Act 2008, with independent review or statutory audit as determined by the Public Interest Score (PIS) Regulations, 2016.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and shareholders of the (Pty) Ltd; CIPC only in cases where filing is mandated (public/state-owned companies or audited companies required by regulation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be completed within 6 months after the financial year-end (s30(1)), approved by the board, signed by a director and presented to the shareholders.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-preparation is a Companies Act contravention; each defaulting director may be fined and/or imprisoned (up to 10 years for serious reckless/false conduct under s216); reportable irregularities must be lodged with CIPC by the auditor/reviewer; persistent default exposes the company to compliance notices, shareholder remedies and lending/underwriting defaults.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory when the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 or more at financial year-end. PIS equals: 1 point per employee, plus 1 point per ZAR 1 million of turnover, plus 1 point per ZAR 1 million of third-party liabilities, plus 1 point per shareholder/beneficial owner. PIS 100–349 requires an independent review; PIS below 100 is exempt unless the MOI, board or shareholders elect otherwise. An e-commerce fast-fashion Pty Ltd with substantial online apparel turnover will cross the 350-point audit threshold once turnover and balance-sheet liabilities exceed the scoring bands.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS Accounting Standards (IASB) are the governing framework for audited South African companies; IFRS for SMEs is permitted for Pty Ltd entities below the public-interest audit threshold; there is no separate national SA GAAP recognised under the Companies Act or IRBA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At the date of each Annual Return the directors must verify and confirm that the Beneficial Ownership Register is complete and accurate. On any shareholding transfer, the Register of Members (securities register) must be updated within 5 business days of receipt of the transfer notice; the BOR must then be amended and the CoR 40.1/CoR 40.2 notification filed with CIPC within 10 business days of the amendment. The Annual Return repeats the final beneficial-ownership position, and a clean filing is impossible while a BOR notification remains outstanding.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 90 – 450 per annum (ZAR 1,700 – 8,500) for registered office/address agent and annual-return secretarial administration in Johannesburg, Cape Town or Durban.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,700 – 8,000 per annum (ZAR 50,000 – 150,000) for a statutory audit of a mid-size e-commerce Pty Ltd; an independent review typically costs USD 800 – 1,700; B-BBEE and other assurance work is additional.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (normal corporate income tax rate for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No bespoke tax holiday for e-commerce retail. General reliefs applicable to a (Pty) Ltd fast-fashion retailer: (i) approved Special Economic Zone (SEZ) companies taxed at an effective 15% rate on qualifying SEZ activities; (ii) enhanced Research and Development deduction of 150% under s11D where qualifying software or logistics-related R&D is conducted; (iii) Employment Tax Incentive (ETI) for qualifying employees under 30 earning below the statutory threshold; (iv) learnership and artisan allowances under s12H; and (v) renewable energy and energy-efficiency capital allowances under s12B/s12BA. The clothing and footwear electronic retailing business does not ordinarily qualify for SEZ or R&D incentives unless delivery robotics or fulfilment software development is ring-fenced as approved research.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (assessed losses are carried forward indefinitely under s20 of the Income Tax Act; no 5-year expiry applies. However, s20A suspends the loss in respect of a company that is not carrying on a trade, including a dormant intermediate holding company, so an active fast-fashion e-commerce trade must be maintained to utilise the loss).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) submitted electronically through the South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling portal at www.sarsefiling.co.za; provisional tax estimates and payments are filed on IRP6 through the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with two compulsory provisional tax returns (IRP6) per year of assessment and an optional third top-up estimate due six months after year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual ITR14 must be filed within 12 months after the company's financial year-end, e.g., for a year-end of 29 February 2024, the return is due no later than 28 February 2025. Provisional tax deadlines for a February year-end: first IRP6 estimate by the last business day of August; second IRP6 estimate by the last business day of February; top-up estimate by the last business day of September (six months after year-end). SARS may raise estimated assessments for failure to submit a return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SARS income tax reference number, Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) registration number, registered address, trading address, contact details, and year of assessment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record the South African SARS tax reference number of the Pty (Ltd); identify the ultimate non-resident parent and its country of tax residence in the related-party disclosure sections. A non-resident beneficial owner does not file the ITR14 itself unless the South African company is a branch of a foreign resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part B - Activities and Trade Classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code, description of goods sold, e-commerce platform details, inventory sourcing model, and issuer of cards/payment processors used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the SARS trade classification approximating ISIC 4791 (electronic retailing of apparel); state expressly that the business is 'fast-fashion apparel and footwear online retail'; disclose settlement processed through Klarna BNPL and Shopify Payments so that the SARS auditor can reconcile merchant settlement statements with declared turnover.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part C - Gross Income and Turnover
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover from online apparel sales net of VAT, settlement discounts, credits and returns; separate domestic sales from export sales; disclose any ancillary income such as influencer commissions or platform subsidies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include e-commerce sales settled by BNPL instalments in full at the point of sale; do not defer recognition of Klarna-settled amounts to cash-based dates; attach marketplace and gateway payout statements where annual cross-border settlements exceed ZAR 10 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part D - Cost of Sales and Inventory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening inventory, closing inventory, purchases of apparel and footwear, freight, import duties, warehousing, last-mile delivery, fulfilment costs, payment processor fees, chargebacks and returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If inventory is acquired from a foreign related-party sourcing or manufacturing affiliate, record the price actually paid and add back in Part H the amount by which the price exceeds an arm's length price; retain SARS Customs SAD500 import declarations as audit evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part E - Allowances and Deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing and advertising spend, cloud hosting, software and licence fees, courier and returns-handling costs, bank charges, professional fees, administrative expenses and fixed asset allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibles must satisfy the s23(a) trade requirement and the s23(g) 'expenditure actually incurred' requirement; any management, IP or software royalty paid to the foreign parent must be supported by a written agreement, foreign invoice, economic substance evidence and an arm's length benchmark.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part G - Assessed Loss and Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior years, current-year taxable income or loss, set-off of loss, taxable income, normal tax at 27%, rebates for provisional tax paid and any foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The assessed loss of the Pty (Ltd) may only be set off against current taxable income if the same trade, being active fast-fashion e-commerce, continues; a dormant interposed shell company cannot utilise a suspended loss under s20A; non-resident shareholders are not entitled to personal set-off of company losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part H - Related-Party and Transfer Pricing Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of related parties, country of residence, nature and value of cross-border transactions (purchases, loans, royalties, service fees), transfer-pricing method used, and arm's length outcome.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A complete Transfer Pricing Policy and Local File must be contemporaneous where aggregate affected cross-border transactions exceed ZAR 10 million per year; provide a Master File for multinational groups with consolidated revenue at or above ZAR 1 billion; SARS may issue a notice under s31 of the Income Tax Act and s29 of the Tax Administration Act requiring production of documentation within 60 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: ITR14 Part J - Dividend Withholding Tax (DWT) Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends declared during the year, amounts paid to residents and non-residents, beneficial owner declarations, DWT at 20% or reduced treaty rates, DWT payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent that is beneficial owner of the shares must deliver a signed SARS-prescribed declaration together with an original or certified tax residence certificate (TRC) to the withholding agent before the dividend payment date; in the absence of valid treaty documents, DWT must be withheld at 20%, and the non-resident must claim any refund from SARS under s47G.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the ITR14 or IRP6 by the statutory deadline triggers administrative non-compliance penalties under s210 and s211 of the Tax Administration Act, including a per-day penalty of up to ZAR 250 in respect of a company and a percentage-of-tax component where the tax is determinable, plus interest at the prescribed rate (repo rate plus 3%) on outstanding tax. Deliberate non-filing or submission of a false return is a criminal offence carrying a fine and/or imprisonment of up to two years. Understatement penalties of up to 125% of the shortfall may be imposed for intentional tax evasion; SARS may issue an estimated assessment or a jeopardy assessment where collection is at risk.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% final dividend withholding tax (DWT) on the value of dividends paid by a South African resident company to non-resident beneficial owners. The shareholder is not subject to further normal tax on the dividend in South Africa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Pty (Ltd) or the regulated intermediary before payment: (i) a written declaration confirming beneficial ownership of the shares on the form prescribed by SARS, and (ii) a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign revenue authority. The withholding agent retains the documents, submits the required dividend notification to SARS eFiling, applies the treaty rate (commonly 5% for beneficial owners controlling at least 10% of voting power and 10% for other direct equity holders, with certain treaties providing 0% or other rates), and remits the net DWT to SARS. Where valid treaty documents are obtained only after payment, the 20% DWT withheld may be reclaimed exclusively by the beneficial owner by way of a refund application to SARS in precise conformity with the position adopted under s47G; the local company has no subsequent adjustment right on behalf of the foreign shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory royalty withholding tax of 15% applies to royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates typically range from 0% to 12%. Statutory interest withholding tax of 15% applies to interest paid from a South African source to non-resident lenders; treaty rates commonly range from 0% to 10%. A similar declaration and TRC protocol applies before treaty relief is recognised. For fast-fashion e-commerce groups, a royalty paid to a low-substance Hong Kong, UAE or Mauritius brand-holding affiliate will attract SARS challenge, denial of treaty benefit and, potentially, disallowance of the deduction in full.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File must be prepared and maintained contemporaneously where the aggregate annual value of cross-border affected transactions between the South African company and its non-resident related parties exceeds ZAR 10 million, with a Master File additionally required for multinational groups whose consolidated global revenue is at or above ZAR 1 billion. Country-by-Country reporting and notification obligations arise where the consolidated group revenue is at or above ZAR 10 billion. SARS may direct production of the documentation within 60 days without requiring a formal audit, and failure to produce contemporaneous records elevates the understatement penalty category. A de minimis practical tolerance is applied only where cross-border affected transactions are immaterial, but the e-commerce sourcing model described in this whitepaper will generally exceed the threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute of the type enacted in UAE or Bermuda; instead, substance is tested through the general anti-avoidance rule (s80A to s80L of the Income Tax Act), the controlled foreign company provisions (s9D), the beneficial-ownership requirement in each tax treaty, and the earnings-based interest limitation in s23M (which restricts net interest expense to 30% of tax EBITDA for companies in a controlled group). A fast-fashion retail structure that interposes an offshore brand-owning, financing or procurement company without local premises, qualified full-time employees, managerial independence and substantive risk-bearing activity will be disregarded or re-characterised; the respective sales, logistics and royalty income will be reconstructed as taxable income of the South African operating Pty (Ltd), with DWT imposed on any consequence distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-recording Klarna BNPL settlement receivables or Shopify Payments gross sales; omitting chargebacks, refunds and third-party marketplace revenue; inflating imported inventory purchases from a related Chinese or Hong Kong supplier without valid import documentation; destroying or failing to retain accounting records for the mandatory five-year period; creating duplicate or shell supplier invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Understatement penalty up to 125% of the additional tax under s222 and s223 of the Tax Administration Act; interest at the prescribed rate on the full shortfall; criminal conviction under s234 and s235 of the Tax Administration Act carrying a fine and/or imprisonment up to two years per count; potential prosecution for common-law fraud where false returns are submitted with intent to prejudice SARS; administrative non-compliance penalties and jeopardy assessments for collection protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ITR14 returns or direct the underreporting of e-commerce revenue face criminal prosecution as principals; SARS can invoke the representative-taxpayer doctrine to recover unpaid VAT, PAYE and provisional tax personally from directors where the company failed to comply with its withholding or filing duties; courts may pierce the corporate veil under s77 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 on grounds of reckless/wrongful trading; SARS may seek travel prohibition orders preventing directors from leaving South Africa while a serious tax debt is outstanding, and civil restorative claims may reach personal assets where company assets were dissipated to evade collection.
